newsitem.title: ITALY: German budget key for future investment - Tietmeyer.
newsitem.headline: German budget key for future investment - Tietmeyer.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said the outcome of the government's budget discussions needed to convince investors Germany would remain competitive in the future.

Tietmeyer told a news conference at this Italian lakeside resort that forthcoming discussions in the German parliament were crucial for the future of investment in the country and therefore for its economic recovery.
The first reading of the government's 1997 draft budget is slated for the forthcoming week in the lower house of parliament and a vote on the package is due in November.
"It is very important the outcome is a convincing one because that would increase the expectations that Germany will be in future terms also a competitive country," he said.

Tietmeyer, speaking at an business forum here, noted the mark was now no longer as strong as it had been and wage agreements were more moderate this year compared with last, both of which had a negative effect on economic growth last year.
"These two factors have now disappeared and so we now see a positive result in the export development," he said.

He said he hoped investment in Germany would grow in coming months. "Where there has been a deficiency until now is in the investment area. I hope very much that in the upcoming months in this part there will also be growing demand, but this depends very much on the decisions to be made in the political sector."
"That means in the budget field, in taxation and in social security contributions. These decisions are now in the pipeline," he said.

German gross domestic product (GDP) data for the 1996 second quarter this week showed the economy growing at 1.5 percent on the first quarter and 1.2 percent compared with the same quarter a year ago.

Tietmeyer reiterated that the data themselves were positive but stressed the first quarter had been slow due particularly to bad weather conditions which had negative implications for the construction industry.
"In the construction area there is clearly a late coming effect because of bad weather conditions," he said.
But he said two factors had been relatively positive in the second quarter. Firstly private consumption had been better than expected and secondly exports had improved. He gave no further details.
